instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Venture studio founding and scaling B2B SaaS startups in the supply chain and procurement space. Currently incubating 4 companies at various stages from pre-seed to Series A. In-house team of product designers, engineers, and growth marketers shared across portfolio companies. Evaluating an AI-powered venture thesis validation tool. Enterprise-scale organization with complex multi-layer governance, dedicated innovation/R&D departments, and formal stage-gate project approval processes. We have substantial resources but also significant organizational inertia — aligning stakeholders across divisions takes deliberate effort and senior executive sponsorship.
answers.pastInitiatives: We successfully deployed a new CRM system across the sales team 18 months ago, which improved lead tracking and reduced pipeline data entry time by 30%. The implementation was well-planned with dedicated project management and training. Building on this success, we are now exploring marketing automation integration and AI-assisted lead scoring.
answers.strategicGoals: Growth is our existential mandate. We are losing market share to faster-moving competitors and need to reignite our growth trajectory. We are willing to make significant strategic bets — potentially including M&A, new product lines, or geographic expansion — provided they have a credible path to meaningful revenue contribution within 18 months.
answers.teamSize: Innovation is decentralized across business units, each with its own innovation lead and dedicated resources, coordinated by a group-level Chief Innovation Officer. The total innovation workforce is approximately 100 people across the organization. A group innovation fund of €5M annually is allocated competitively — business units pitch for funding against clear innovation KPIs including revenue from new products and process efficiency gains.
answers.additionalContext: We have a new CEO who joined 3 months ago from a more digitally mature industry. She has signaled that innovation and digital transformation will be top strategic priorities, replacing the previous leadership's conservative, cost-cutting orientation. The organization is cautiously optimistic but also uncertain about what concrete changes to expect.

input.changes_since_last: Restructured leadership team. 8 legacy processes automated. Exploring new revenue streams.

opportunities.title: Standardizing AI-Powered Venture Thesis Validation & Governance Overlay
opportunities.rationale: The evaluation of an AI tool represents a massive opportunity to accelerate decision velocity. To maximize this, the core process needs standardization across all incubated companies. This radical shift requires creating a central governance layer that validates not only technical feasibility but also regulatory compliance before market deployment.

first_actions: Establish a cross-functional AI Governance Committee (legal, tech, domain experts) to define compliance boundaries for new predictive models.
Develop and pilot the minimum viable product (MVP) framework for the AI thesis validation tool, focusing on input standardization.
Audit existing portfolio companies' data handling practices against anticipated regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR, industry-specific mandates).
resources_needed: Sponsorship from the new CEO level
execution_plan.success_metric: Time reduction in venture validation cycle by 40% while maintaining a compliance score above 95%.
milestones: Governance Committee charter signed and operational within 6 weeks.
AI MVP prototype deployed for internal testing on one pilot company.
Formalized AI Usage Policy communicated to all business unit leaders.

opportunities.title: Implementing a Unified, Portfolio-Level Growth Strategy Operating Model
opportunities.rationale: The current decentralized innovation process creates 'siloed' growth bets and impedes strategic capital allocation. A radical change is needed to shift from competitive funding pitches (internal competition) to a unified model where central leadership guides high-potential market adjacencies, ensuring exponential growth across the entire studio.

first_actions: Executive workshop defining 3-5 core 'pillar' market opportunities for the next 24 months.
Revise the innovation fund allocation process to prioritize strategic synergy over isolated efficiency gains.
Implement standardized Stage-Gate reviews that require proof of multi-division adoption, not just single-unit revenue.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in the number of competing, non-synergistic growth initiatives by 30%.
milestones: New Group Strategy playbook finalized and approved.
First cycle of portfolio alignment workshops completed with BU leaders.
Metrics updated to track synergy realization rather than just individual unit KPIs.

next_steps.action: Formalize and mandate the cross-functional AI Governance Committee (O2) to address high regulatory risk.
next_steps.owner: Group Chief Innovation Officer / Legal Counsel

next_steps.action: Host a CEO-led 'Future Market Vision' session to align all BU leaders on the top 3 strategic areas for combined growth (O3).
Develop a centralized, formal mechanism to capture and action 'informal conversations' into structured product requirements.

key_weaknesses: Significant organizational inertia requiring continuous, high-level executive sponsorship to overcome siloed decision-making.
Lack of standardized governance structure for new technologies (AI), creating regulatory and compliance risk.
Reliance on informal feedback channels limits scalability and data integrity across the portfolio.

improvements: Successfully automated 8 legacy processes, demonstrating operational efficiency gains.
Implemented a robust CRM system improving lead tracking and reducing manual data entry time by 30%.
Increased digital maturity by moving from ad-hoc optimization to structured planning (e.g., exploring marketing automation).
persistent_gaps: The core barrier remains structural alignment across business units, preventing the full realization of strategic bets.
Formalized customer feedback loops are still insufficient; reliance on 'informal conversations' is a scaling risk.
Governance processes are highly varied by project/BU, leading to inconsistent compliance and operational standards.
achieved_milestones: Successful deployment and adoption of the new CRM system across the sales team.
Establishment of dedicated R&D departments focused on specific technology stacks (e.g., AI).

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: Significant structural and operational improvements have been achieved (CRM deployment, process automation). The leadership has signaled a shift from cost-cutting to aggressive growth bets, materially increasing the organization's risk appetite and strategic ambition.
